entities.name: Kalinga Magha
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kalinga Magha, also known as Gangaraja Kalinga Vijayabahu, was the ruler who usurped the throne of Parakrama Pandyan II of Polonnaruwa in 1215, prompting a massive migration of Sinhalese people to the south and west of Sri Lanka and into the mountainous interior.

This event marked the beginning of the end of the traditional northern seat of native power on the island, known as Rajarata, and had far-reaching consequences for the politics, culture, and demographics of Sri Lanka.

The legacy of Kalinga Magha can be seen in the ongoing struggles for power and identity in Sri Lanka, as well as the complex cultural dynamics between the Sinhalese and other ethnic groups on the island.

As the last ruler to hold his seat in the traditional northern seat of power, Magha's actions had a profound impact on the course of Sri Lankan history, shaping the island's politics, culture, and identity for centuries to come.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kalinga Magha's invasion of Polonnaruwa in 1215 marked a significant turning point in Sri Lankan history, leading to the mass migration of Sinhalese people and the destruction of the traditional northern seat of native power on the island.
